p11-l02.q: Samples per bit at 16× oversampling for a transmitter 3 % slow?

p11-l02.explain: Past samples 151 and 152, so the vote reads the previous data bit.

p11-l02.q: Drift of the stop-bit centre in samples at 3 % baud error (16×, 8N1)?
Sample rate in Hz for 16× oversampling at 115 200 baud?
The line is high at the middle of a detected start bit. What does the receiver do?
options: treats it as a glitch and returns to idle

p11-l02.q: What does a majority vote of three samples reject?
p11-l02.explain: Two adjacent bad samples still win the vote.

p11-l03.q: Fraction of 17-bit bursts a CRC-16 misses, as 1 in how many?

options: because E(1) = 1 for odd weight, which a multiple of (x+1) can’t be

p11-l04.q: Worst-case encoded length (without the delimiter) of a 508-byte packet?
p11-l04.explain: Two FF blocks of 254, then a final 01 code for the empty last block.

p11-l04.q: Percentage overhead of COBS for long packets in the worst case?
Encoded length of a packet of 300 zeros?
p11-l04.explain: Each zero becomes code 01, plus a final 01.

p11-l04.q: The code byte for “two data bytes, then a zero”?
What does the code byte FF mean?
options: 254 data bytes and no zero after them

p11-l04.q: Why do COBS frames still need a CRC?
p11-l04.explain: A flipped bit decodes to a wrong but well-formed packet.
options: COBS finds packet boundaries but doesn’t detect corrupted bytes

p11-l05.q: One 8E1 character time at 19 200 baud, in µs?
The 3.5-character silence at 9600 baud with 11-bit characters, in ms?
p11-l05.explain: Below 19 200 baud it scales with the baud rate.

p11-l05.q: Response length in bytes for reading 10 registers with function 03?
p11-l05.explain: Address, function, byte count, 20 data bytes, 2 CRC bytes.

p11-l05.q: Load in ohms seen by the driver from two 120 Ω terminators?
p11-l05.explain: The standard’s 54 Ω also allows for the receivers.

p11-l05.q: A slave answers function 03 with function code 0x83 and data 02. What happened?
p11-l05.explain: Top bit set means an exception; code 02 is illegal data address.

p11-l05.q: Why does RS-485 survive ground shifts that break a plain UART?
options: the receiver looks only at the difference between A and B, within a wide common-mode range

SCL falls while SDA is high

p11-l06.q: Why can a slave stretch the clock?
p11-l06.explain: The master releases SCL and waits until it actually rises.
options: SCL is open drain, so holding it low makes the master wait

p11-l07.q: Temperature in °C for a raw reading of 0?

Rate in °/s for a raw gyro reading of 1000 at ±500 °/s?

options: the chip latches them, so all values come from one sample

p11-l07.q: What does the recorded-dump test catch that a fake returning fixed values doesn’t?
p11-l07.explain: It checks every transaction against what the real chip saw.
options: wrong registers, wrong order or extra bus accesses

p11-l08.q: Maximum SCK in MHz with t_pd = 1 ns, t_co = 8 ns and t_su = 3 ns?

both sample on rising edges, and many slaves detect the idle clock level at CS fall

p11-l09.explain: Conversion plus the word plus the gap.

p11-l09.q: Timer reload value (ARR) for 250 kS/s from 84 MHz?

p11-l09.explain: A circular DMA never waits for the CPU.

p11-l10.q: Maximum cable length in m at 500 kbit/s (75 % sample point, 5 ns/m, 150 ns transceivers)?
p11-l10.explain: The round trip must fit before the sample point.

p11-l10.q: Duration in µs of a 111-bit frame at 500 kbit/s?
Bus load in percent from one 111-bit frame every 1 ms at 500 kbit/s?

p11-l10.explain: The first bit where they differ, counting from the MSB.
No bandwidth is lost to the collision.
